verses.zh: （大卫的诗，交与伶长。）眷顾贫穷的有福了！他遭难的日子，耶和华必搭救他。
verses.en: For the music director, a psalm of David.How blessed[NOTE:1] is the one who treats the poor properly.[NOTE:2] When trouble comes,[NOTE:3] may[NOTE:4] the Lord deliver him.[NOTE:5]
notes: Psalm 41. The psalmist is confident (vv. 11-12) that the Lord has heard his request to be healed (vv. 4-10), and he anticipates the joy he will experience when the Lord intervenes (vv. 1-3). One must assume that the psalmist is responding to a divine oracle of assurance (see P. C. Craigie, Psalms 1-50 [WBC], 319-20). The final verse is a fitting conclusion to this psalm, but it is also serves as a fitting conclusion to the first “book” (or major editorial division) of the Psalter. Similar statements appear at or near the end of each of the second, third, and fourth “books” of the Psalter (see Pss 72:19; 89:52, and 106:48 respectively).

The Hebrew noun is an abstract plural. The word often refers metonymically to the happiness that God-given security and prosperity produce (see Pss 1:1, 3; 2:12; 34:9; 65:4; 84:12; 89:15; 106:3; 112:1; 127:5; 128:1; 144:15).

One who treats the poor properly. The psalmist is characterizing himself as such an individual and supplying a reason why God has responded favorably to his prayer. The Lord’s attitude toward the merciful mirrors their treatment of the poor.
Heb “in the day of trouble” (see Ps 27:5).

The prefixed verb יְמַלְּטֵהוּ (yemalletehu) has the form of the pronominal suffix typical of the jussive not the imperfect (יְמַלְּטֶנּוּ, yemalletennu). The jussive form continues throughout the next verse. The principle that begins v. 1 is the basis for the petition in vv. 1b-2. Verse 3 transitions to a statement of confidence and testimony.

verses.zh: 耶和华必保全他，使他存活；他必在地上享福。求你不要把他交给仇敌，遂其所愿。
verses.en: May the Lord protect him and save his life.[NOTE:1] May he be blessed[NOTE:2] in the land.Do not turn him over[NOTE:3] to his enemies.[NOTE:4]
notes: That is, the one who has been kind to the poor.

The prefixed verbal forms are taken as jussives in the translation because of the form of the pronominal suffix (-ehu rather than -ennu) and because the jussive is clearly used in the final line of the verse.

The translation follows the consonantal Hebrew text (Kethib), which has a Pual (passive) prefixed form, regarded here as a jussive. The Pual of the verb אָשַׁר (ʾashar) also appears in Prov 3:18. The marginal reading (Qere) assumes a vav (ו) consecutive and Pual perfect. Some, with the support of the LXX, change the verb to a Piel (active) form with an objective pronominal suffix, “and may he bless him,” or “and he will bless him” (cf. NIV84).

The negative particle אַל (ʾal) before the prefixed verbal form indicates the verb is a jussive and the statement a prayer. Those who want to take v. 2 as a statement of confidence suggest emending the negative particle to לֹא (loʾ), which is used with the imperfect. See the earlier note on the verbal forms in line one of this verse. According to GKC 322 §109.e, this is a case where the jussive is used rhetorically to “express that something cannot or should not happen.” In this case one might translate, “you will not turn him over to his enemies,” and take the preceding verbal forms as indicative in mood. However, none of the examples offered in GKC for this use of the jussive are compelling.

verses.zh: 他病重在榻，耶和华必扶持他；他在病中，你必给他铺床。
verses.en: The Lord supports[NOTE:1] him on his sickbed;you have healed him from his illness.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “do not give him over to the desire of his enemies” (see Ps 27:12).

The prefixed verbal form could be taken as jussive, continuing the prayer of v. 2, but the parallel line in v. 3b employs the perfect, suggesting that the psalmist is again speaking in the indicative mood (see v. 1b). The imperfect can be understood as future or as generalizing (see v. 1).

verses.zh: 我曾说：耶和华啊，求你怜恤我，医治我！因为我得罪了你。
verses.en: As for me, I said:[NOTE:1] “O Lord, have mercy on me!Heal me, for I have sinned against you.
notes: Heb “all his bed you have changed in his illness.” The perfect verb may indicate a testimony of what God has done in the past as part of the statement of confidence.

verses.zh: 我的仇敌用恶言议论我说：他几时死，他的名才灭亡呢？
verses.en: My enemies ask this cruel question about me,[NOTE:1] ‘When will he finally die and be forgotten?’[NOTE:2]
notes: In vv. 4-10 the psalmist recites the prayer of petition and lament he offered to the Lord.
Heb “my enemies speak evil concerning me.”

verses.zh: 他来看我就说假话；他心存奸恶，走到外边才说出来。
verses.en: When someone comes to visit,[NOTE:1] he pretends to be friendly;[NOTE:2] he thinks of ways to defame me,[NOTE:3] and when he leaves he slanders me.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “and his name perish.”
Heb “to see.”
Heb “he speaks deceitfully.”
Heb “his heart gathers sin to itself.”

verses.zh: 一切恨我的，都交头接耳地议论我；他们设计要害我。
verses.en: All who hate me whisper insults about me to one another;[NOTE:1] they plan ways to harm me.
notes: Heb “he goes outside and speaks.”

verses.zh: 他们说：有怪病贴在他身上；他已躺卧，必不能再起来。
verses.en: They say,[NOTE:1] ‘An awful disease[NOTE:2] overwhelms him,[NOTE:3] and now that he is bedridden he will never recover.’[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “together against me they whisper, all those who hate me.” The Hitpael of לָחַשׁ (lakhash) refers here to whispering to one another (see 2 Sam 12:19).
The words “they say” are not in the Hebrew text, but are supplied in the translation to make it clear that v. 8 contains a quotation of what the psalmist’s enemies say about him (see v. 7a).
Heb “thing of worthlessness.” In Ps 101:3 the phrase refers to evil deeds in general, but here it appears to refer more specifically to the illness that plagues the psalmist.
Heb “is poured out on him.” The passive participle of יָצַק (yatsaq) is used.

verses.zh: 连我知己的朋友，我所倚靠、吃过我饭的也用脚踢我。
verses.en: Even my close friend[NOTE:1] whom I trusted,he who shared meals with me, has turned against me.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “and he who lies down will not again arise.”
Heb “man of my peace.” The phrase here refers to one’s trusted friend (see Jer 38:22; Obad 7).

verses.zh: 耶和华啊，求你怜恤我，使我起来，好报复他们！
verses.en: As for you, O Lord, have mercy on me and raise me up,so I can pay them back!”[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “has made a heel great against me.” The precise meaning of this phrase, which appears only here, is uncertain.sn The language of this verse is applied to Judas Iscariot in John 13:18.

verses.zh: 因我的仇敌不得向我夸胜，我从此便知道你喜爱我。
verses.en: By this[NOTE:1] I know that you are pleased with me,for my enemy does[NOTE:2] not triumph[NOTE:3] over me.
notes: The cohortative with prefixed vav (ו) here indicates purpose or result (“Then I will repay them”) after the preceding imperatives.

By this. Having recalled his former lament and petition, the psalmist returns to the confident mood of vv. 1-3. The basis for his confidence may be a divine oracle of deliverance, assuring him that God would intervene and vindicate him. The demonstrative pronoun “this” may refer to such an oracle, which is assumed here, though its contents are not included. See P. C. Craigie, Psalms 1-50 (WBC), 319, 321.
Or “will.” One may translate the imperfect verbal form as descriptive (present, cf. NIV) or as anticipatory (future, cf. NEB).

verses.zh: 你因我纯正就扶持我，使我永远站在你的面前。
verses.en: As for me, you uphold[NOTE:1] me because of my integrity;[NOTE:2] you allow[NOTE:3] me permanent access to your presence.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “shout.”
Or “have upheld.” The perfect verbal form can be taken as generalizing/descriptive (present) or as a present perfect.
Because of my integrity. See Pss 7:8; 25:21; 26:1, 11.

The prefixed verbal form with vav (ו) consecutive has the same aspectual function as the preceding perfect. It is either generalizing/descriptive (present) or has a present perfect nuance (“you have allowed”).

verses.zh: 耶和华―以色列的　神是应当称颂的，从亘古直到永远。阿们！阿们！
verses.en: The Lord God of Israel deserves praise[NOTE:1] in the future and forevermore.[NOTE:2] We agree! We agree![NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “and you cause me to stand before you permanently.”
Heb “[be] blessed.” See Pss 18:46; 28:6; 31:21.
Heb “from everlasting to everlasting.” See 1 Chr 16:36; Neh 9:5; Pss 90:2; 106:48.
